# The strategy — RULED 2026-09-29

AI carries a data source from ingestion to a served layer, generates the first ontology and everything around it, and then — against domain questions whose answers a subject-matter expert has approved — tunes the ontology's declarations in a loop until the generator produces sound SQL for every one of them. The console is the central place where all of it is created, authored and seen. A person rules; AI proposes, measures, drafts and iterates.

**This page describes the present.** It is generated from `guardrails/strategy.yaml`, the one home of the strategy; `tools/check_strategy.py` holds every name on it to what exists and reports which rung a bundle has reached; the framework gate runner holds the rungs' gates on every delivery.

## Stop condition

Every domain question in the bundle's corpus passes against its SME-approved answer, and the framework gate runner reports no NEWS — every remaining red is a declared, owned standing failure.

## Principles

- **declarations-not-code** — Every behaviour of the answer comes from the ontology's declarations — concepts, rules, rulings, registers, edges — never from generator code or per-question prompts. The loop tunes declarations.  
  *Because:* the grammar was measured not to be the bottleneck (70 of 70 questions encoded; the declarations were); code patched per question overfits the corpus.
- **vocabulary-is-the-frameworks** — The closed vocabularies (mac_vocabulary.yaml) are the framework's and are read, never restated. A bundle tunes its USE of them. A missing term is a framework proposal, not a bundle tweak.  
  *Because:* one fact in six homes is how `attribute` stayed alive for two days after its retirement.
- **ai-proposes-a-person-ratifies** — Rule confidence P→C, register and DQ dispositions, transform drivers `ruled`, and approved answers are a person's acts. The composer never stamps C; the guard lets an agent describe and only a human dispose.  
  *Because:* a generator certifying its own output reads as a ratified fact to anyone who did not check.
- **whole-corpus-per-change** — A change made for one question is re-run against every question. Fixing question 12 must not break 1–11.  
  *Because:* a corpus is the specification; a single question is a test case.
- **a-red-gate-stops-something** — Every non-green gate is declared with an owner (tools/gate_register.py) or it is news, and news exits 1. There is no bare PASS over standing failures.  
  *Because:* a runner that was red continuously switched nothing.
- **one-home-per-fact** — A fact is declared once and generated everywhere else (schema enums from the vocabulary, the manual's term blocks, this document).  
  *Because:* two homes that may disagree will.

## The ladder

| rung | what AI does | what a person does |
|---|---|---|
| 1 · **ingest** | ingests the sources — describes each landing relation, profiles it (distincts, nulls, singletons), cuts samples, measures references and keys, cuts value-set registers | disposes the registers' findings (only a human disposes; an agent may describe) |
| 2 · **analyse-and-transform** | analyses the sources — raises data-quality findings with a recommendation each, traces lineage, drafts the first transformation as a 1:1 passthrough and PROPOSES improvements where the profiling shows them (`driven_by: passthrough | proposed | ruled` on the .sql) | rules each finding; an SME or data scientist drives the `ruled` transforms |
| 3 · **serve** | establishes the served layer — applies the transforms, describes the datasets, promotes them, writes the delivery manifest and checks the delivery's consistency | approves the data plane |
| 4 · **dependencies** | creates everything the ontology will lean on — SME questions from the findings, the data-quality board, the sanity suite, measured edges, the ER diagram | the SME answers the questions in the trilateral channel |
| 5 · **first-ontology** | generates the first ontology from the rows — the centre found in the data, one concept per notion (A2 decides the class), rules in the six kinds, rulings measured before ruled, edges as verbs — and keeps the modelling log of its line of thought | reads the log, rules confidence P→C, answers the SME questions the model raises |
| 6 · **supporting-objects** | generates every derived object the console shows — objects.json, concept pages, the edges projection, concept samples, the ER and lineage graphs, the resource description | none — derived, never authored |
| 7 · **console** | none — the console is where a person creates, authors and sees; AI works behind its surfaces | the operator and the SME work here — every rung has a surface; authoring from the console goes through the one SSOT writer and the guard |
| 8 · **questions** | none — the questions are the domain's; AI renders them into the test framework | the SME poses the domain questions |
| 9 · **answer-and-approve** | answers each question by direct, read-only access to the data — resolution ladder, no guessed endpoint — and presents the number with its evidence | the SME approves the answer; pass/fail is the only verdict, and the approved number is the reference |
| 10 · **configure** | configures the ontology for each approved question with the framework's vocabulary and grammar — rules, rulings, registers, edges, surfaces — so the planner produces sound SQL from declarations alone | ratifies the rules it changes (confidence C) and the dispositions it needs |
| 11 · **loop** | runs over every question — identifies the correct answer, diagnoses which declarations fired and which were missing, tunes them, re-runs the whole corpus — until every approved question passes | none per iteration; ratification as in rung 10; the stop condition is theirs to call |

## Documentation

A document describes the PRESENT. History lives in protocol/ (append-only) and in CONFORMANCE §6 (the changelog); a proposal says PROPOSED on its first line; a document that narrates a past state is marked history or retired by the citation rule (cited by no gate, tool, guardrail, wiki claim or README, and describing a shape the schema no longer routes).

Enforced by: `tools/check_dangling_references.py`, `tools/check_retired_terms.py`, `tools/gen_strategy.py`, `tools/gen_vocabulary_terms.py`.  
**Owed:** a `describes: current | history | proposal` front-matter ratchet over every hand-written page, so a page that narrates the past says so on its face.
